name: AI Security and Red Teaming
summary: AI systems fail in new ways. Learn to attack your own before someone else does — and to defend them.
prerequisites: Requires prompt engineering. No offensive security background assumed.
syllabus: How LLM applications fail and how they are attacked
Red teaming: planning, executing and reporting
Defences: filters, tool isolation and human review
topics: The attack surface of an LLM application
Direct prompt injection: getting around the system instructions
Indirect injection: malicious content in pages, files and emails
Jailbreaks and policy evasion
Leaking the system prompt and sensitive data
Poisoning data and vector stores
Tool misuse and excessive agent permissions
Hallucination as a security and business risk
Bias and fairness: where they come from and how to measure them
OWASP Top 10 for LLM applications
Red teaming: scope, rules of engagement and written authorisation
Planning test scenarios and adversarial cases
Automating adversarial tests and measuring the failure rate
The red team report for a model: the prompt that worked, and how often it does
Defences: input and output validation, allowlists and filters
Content moderation APIs
Identifying the end user in model calls (end-user IDs)
Knowing your customer and the use case before opening up the model
Restricting inputs and outputs: schemas, allowlists and limits
Tool isolation, least privilege and human confirmation
Logging prompts and outputs: what to keep, what to redact, and for how long
Brazil’s LGPD applied to data sent to third-party models
